reuse.why: The range rule is updated in the shared getScheduledAmount, but the API's expectedAmount is computed by a new local getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of calling that helper, and the approximate-amount rule is added only there.

duplication.why: getExpectedScheduleAmount in api-models.ts re-implements the missing-amount and range (Math.min) logic already in getScheduledAmount, so the expected-amount rule now has two definitions.

placement.why: The approximate worst-case rule lives in the API model layer rather than in shared/schedules.ts, so posting, previews, forecasts, templates and the UI never apply it.

scope.why: Changes stay on the expected-amount rule, its comments and tests, though comment rewrites are somewhat garbled.

maintainability.why: Two diverging definitions of the expected amount (API vs everything else) will drift further; the now-pointless round parameter of the shared helper is kept.

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount is a renamed, reshaped copy of getScheduledAmount (null => 0, number passthrough, Math.min of range) with an extra isapprox branch

abstraction_drift.where: scheduleModel.toExternal calls a local getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of the shared getScheduledAmount; the isapprox rule exists only in that bypass
